final_answer:
SUPPLY AND DEMAND DETERMINE PRICE IN A FREE MARKET THROUGH THEIR INTERACTION. DEMAND REPRESENTS HOW MUCH CONSUMERS WANT A GOOD/SERVICE AT DIFFERENT PRICES, GENERALLY FALLING AS PRICE RISES. SUPPLY REPRESENTS HOW MUCH PRODUCERS ARE WILLING TO PROVIDE, OFTEN INCREASING AS PRICE RISES. THE MARKET EQUILIBRIUM PRICE OCCURS WHERE SUPPLY EQUALS DEMAND. IF PRICE IS ABOVE EQUILIBRIUM, SURPLUS EXISTS (SUPPLY EXCEEDS DEMAND), PRESSING PRICES DOWNWARD. IF BELOW EQUILIBRIUM, SHORTAGE EXISTS (DEMAND EXCEEDS SUPPLY), PRESSING PRICES UPWARD. THIS DYNAMIC ADJUSTMENT SETS THE MARKET PRICE.  

WHEN A GOVERNMENT IMPOSES A PRICE CEILING (A MAXIMUM LEGAL PRICE), IT CAN DISTORT THIS MECHANISM. IF THE CEILING IS SET BELOW THE EQUILIBRIUM PRICE, SUPPLIERS REDUCE PRODUCTION (LOWER PROFITS OR UNVIABLE MARGINS) WHILE DEMAND REMAINS HIGH, CREATE A SHORTAGE. THIS LEADS TO QUEUING, BLACK MARKETS, REDUCED QUALITY, OR SHORTER AVAILABILITY. IF THE CEILING IS ABOVE EQUILIBRIUM, IT HAS NO EFFECT. PRICE CEILINGS OFTEN INTEND TO MAKE GOODS AFFORDABLE BUT CAN DEGRADE MARKET EFFICIENCY.
